title: How antihelminthic drugs act on worms
ariaLabel: Schematic of four ways drugs act on worms: benzimidazoles block tubulin so the worm cannot take up glucose, ivermectin opens glutamate-gated chloride channels and paralyses the worm, praziquantel raises calcium in the worm's surface and causes spastic paralysis, and pyrantel activates nicotinic receptors and causes spastic paralysis.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or lipid value is shown or implied.
blockInfo: A drug of the chosen class acting at this step (generic teaching symbol, not a named drug's shape). Less passes here, with the effects shown at the cholesterol and the LDL receptors.

nodes.label: Tubulin
nodes.info: Microtubules of the worm's gut cells, needed to take up glucose.

nodes.label: Glucose uptake
nodes.info: Glucose taken up by the worm.

nodes.label: Glutamate signalling
nodes.info: Glutamate-gated chloride channels, found in invertebrates.

nodes.label: Calcium
nodes.info: Calcium movement across the worm's surface layer (tegument).

nodes.label: Surface layer intact
nodes.info: The worm's outer layer protects it from the host immune system.

nodes.label: Acetylcholine signals
nodes.info: Acetylcholine acting on nicotinic receptors of worm muscle.

nodes.label: Muscle control
nodes.info: Controlled contraction of the worm's muscle, needed to hold on in the gut.

nodes.label: Worm survival
nodes.info: A teaching score for the worm's survival and grip on the host.

edges.label: microtubules
edges.info: Albendazole and mebendazole bind worm beta-tubulin and block microtubules, so the worm cannot absorb glucose and slowly starves.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: chloride channel
edges.info: Ivermectin opens glutamate-gated chloride channels, which hyperpolarises and paralyses the worm.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: calcium channels
edges.info: Praziquantel raises calcium entry in schistosomes and tapeworms, causing spastic paralysis and damage to the surface layer.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: nicotinic receptor
edges.info: Pyrantel (and similar drugs) activate nicotinic receptors of worm muscle, causing spastic paralysis, so the worm is expelled.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

sources: Where each class acts. Benzimidazoles block worm tubulin, ivermectin opens glutamate-gated chloride channels, praziquantel increases calcium in the worm surface, and pyrantel activates nicotinic receptors. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: Diethylcarbamazine, niclosamide, which drug suits which worm, tissue and gut parasites, resistance, mass treatment, pregnancy, adverse effects and reactions to dying parasites are left out. Worm survival is drawn as a teaching score. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
